title: Shadow-shift synthesis: SRE weekly narrative - 2027-02-24
content:
Purpose and tone
This is a narrative-style weekly note from the shadow shift/on-call rotation that synthesizes incidents, SLO posture, and immediate runbook/handoff needs. Think of this as the informal but structured log I leave for the next shift and the ENG leads — less polished than the postmortems, more contextual than the ticket titles.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Three visible incidents this week; none required customer-facing SEV escalation but two produced measurable SLO pressure.
- Primary root causes: (1) cross-region routing flaps during a deploy; (2) an aggressive cache TTL change that produced cold-start tail latency; (3) mis-tuned horizontal autoscaler during a burst test.
- Action items: rollout a short-lived traffic-shed policy for canaries, revert the cache TTL and add a smoothing limiter, and update autoscaler runbook with pre-warm hooks.

Incidents (short chronicle)
1) "routing-ripple" — partial 503 spike (2027-02-21 07:42 UTC)
  - Symptom: downstream client errors (503/502) from a subset of gateway nodes for ~9m, 95th latency for the hosted-api route spiked to 2.1s.
  - Impact: ~4% request error rate on the US cluster for the window; no persisted data loss, retries recovered most traffic.
  - Immediate mitigation: rerouted traffic off the affected AZ to healthy pool; engaged oncall-networking for BGP/route verification.
  - Root cause (preliminary): a rolling deploy of the edge proxy introduced a race in upstream health checks; probes marked a small group unhealthy, autoscaler reacted and caused transient reconnections.
  - Follow-ups: add a brief deploy-delay (30s) that gates health-check false-positives; open PR to add a probe jitter to the proxy; create an integration test for rolling update health stability.

2) "cache-thin-slice" — KV cache TTL regression (2027-02-22 03:15 UTC)
  - Symptom: sustained 95th token latency increase for session-based models; per-request cold-starts increased KVMiss by ~6x.
  - Impact: SLO latency breach risk on several customer routes; visible in per-route latency dashboards and a small uptick in support tickets.
  - Immediate mitigation: rolled TTL back to previous value, enabled fast-path cache warming for flagged customers, and paused an automated TTL optimization job.
  - Root cause: an experimental config (automated eviction policy) merged into staging and promoted by mistake to canary without the expected throttle.
  - Follow-ups: tag that optimization job as experimental and require explicit opt-in; add gate to promote experimental infra config; postmortem draft assigned to @Kai.

3) "scale-warmup-lag" — autoscaler underprovisioning during burst test (2027-02-23 11:20 UTC)
  - Symptom: during a planned traffic storm test, several Dedicated pools showed a warmup lag causing queueing at the dispatcher and elevated p95 response times.
  - Impact: internal test failure; minor cost spike due to emergency scale-up. No customer exposure (test routed to test cluster).
  - Immediate mitigation: manual scale-up to required capacity; created a temporary pre-warm task that starts worker processes ahead of traffic.
  - Root cause: autoscaler assumptions (startup time = 45s) were invalid for the new model variant (startup ~120s with quantized weights).
  - Follow-ups: update autoscaler model-profile with measured startup times; ensure autoscaler has a conservative startup baseline; add a pre-warm hook to the rollout process for heavy models.

SLO snapshot (week overview)
- Hosted API overall availability: 99.96% (target 99.99%) — one minor miss window caused a 0.03% deficit.
- 95th token latency (prod routes): 820ms (target 700ms) — driven by cache-thin-slice event.
- Error budget remaining (monthly): ~0.82% (post incidents).
Notes: metric anomalies were concentrated in US-west and in routes that use session caching heavily. We are tracking per-customer impact and will alert key accounts if any regressions persist.

Runbook and tooling updates
- Cache eviction playbook: small rewrite to include an "experiment tag" check before config promote. Draft pushed to PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234.
- Autoscaler runbook: added pre-warm checklist and a startup-time sampling job. Need owner for automated sampling (suggested: Marta).
- Deploy gating: prototype delay/jitter for health probes merged to staging; requires load test to validate.

Operational action items (owners and ETA)
- Rana: schedule deploy-stability load test for edge proxy (ETA 2027-03-03).
- Kai: draft postmortem for cache-thin-slice and propose experimental gating (ETA 2027-02-28).
- Marta: add startup-time sampling job to autoscaler repo and assign dashboard (ETA 2027-03-05).
- Ethan: add canary traffic-shed policy and test in staging (ETA 2027-03-02).
- Oncall: add an explicit checklist step to verify 'experimental' label on infra configs during handoffs.

On-call handoff notes (explicit)
- Next oncall rotation: 2027-02-25 08:00 UTC -> 2027-03-03 08:00 UTC. Primary: Kai Nguyen; Secondary: Marta Ruiz.
- Key things to look for in next 72h: probe jitter deploy (watch probe flaps), cache hit ratio (KVMiss), autoscaler 'startup' metric.
- Handoff tiny checklist (copy into the rotation):
  1) Check SLO dashboard (latency and availability) for red tiles.
  2) Verify no staging-to-prod promo job ran in the last 6h (experimental tag check).
  3) Confirm there is a functioning warmup queue for any scheduled rollouts.
  4) Note any customer escalations in #customer-ops and ping CS lead if >1 customer impacted.

Blameless notes / culture points
- Two of the three incidents were linked to promotions of experimental infra configs or unmeasured assumptions. This is a recurring theme — we should emphasize the "double confirm" rule for infra experiments.
- Reminder: blameless lens in all follow-ups; focus on process fixes (gating, testing, measurement) not individual mistakes.

Meeting and syncs this week
- SRE weekly triage (Thu 09:00 UTC): present cache postmortem draft, autoscaler plan.
- Cross-functional deploy-stability working session (Fri 14:00 UTC): infra + release-eng + serving-runtime.
- Follow-up with CS: ad-hoc sync if customer-facing latencies reappear.

Loose/notes-to-self (scratchpad style)
- Investigate whether KV cache warmers should be moved to async background task vs inline on request. Trade: cost vs latency.
- Consider a small metric: "proxy probe-flap count per deploy" to track rolling update stability.
- Check if the canary traffic shed policy can be automated by the console (product-ops ask).

Open questions
- Do we have a stable way to capture model startup time across all GPU types? Need a single source-of-truth.
- Should experimental infra changes require a 'two-person approve' step if they touch caching or routing logic?

Appendix: short metrics table (last 7d)
- Total requests: 11.3M
- Average p95 latency (prod): 820ms
- Median latency: 120ms
- Error rate (5d rolling): 0.29%
- Cache hit rate (session routes): 84% (dipped to 62% during TTL regression)

Attendees who contributed to this doc
- Rana Patel (author), Kai Nguyen (incident lead), Marta Ruiz (autoscaler), Ethan Brooks (deploys), Priya Shah (observability consult).

If you pick this doc up mid-shift: prioritize cache hit ratio and probe-flap alerts. If both are green, focus on stabilizing the autoscaler sampling job.

End of note.
